test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 01 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The average runs scored by a batsman in 23 matches is 43. In the next 10 matches, the batsman scored an average of 13 runs. Find his average runs scored (rounded off to two decimal places) in all the 33 matches.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **deviation** method: Assume the overall **average** is 43.

For the next 10 **matches**, the deviation is (13 − 43) = −30 per match.

Total **negative deviation** = 10 × (−30) = −300.

Average **reduction** across 33 matches = −300 ÷ 33 ≈ −9.09.

New **average runs** = 43 − 9.09 = 33.91.

**∴ The correct answer is 33.91.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Matches**₁ = 23, **Average**₁ = 43 | **Matches**₂ = 10, **Average**₂ = 13.

**Formula:** **Combined Average** = (Sum of all **runs**) ÷ (Total **matches**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9452cf6d044c2e5edb585a8396a67f83150a3494b6414098e4350872d03b57d1.png] 

⇒ Total **runs** in first 23 **matches** = 23 × 43 = 989

⇒ Total **runs** in next 10 **matches** = 10 × 13 = 130

⇒ Grand total **runs** = 989 + 130 = 1119

⇒ Total **matches** = 23 + 10 = 33

⇒ Overall **average** = 1119 ÷ 33

⇒ Overall **average** ≈ 33.9090...

⇒ Rounded **average** = 33.91

**∴ The correct answer is 33.91.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the **combined average** is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Sum of Observations

The total **sum** of all observations is always calculated as **Average** × Number of **Observations**.

Concept of Net Deviation

In any distribution, the sum of **deviations** of all observations from the **arithmetic mean** is always zero.</p
